title: Bank Statement Formats: MT940, CAMT.053, BAI2, OFX

questions.question: A statement opens at 12,500.00, lists lines of -1,500.00, +3,250.75, and -12.50, and closes at 14,283.25. What does that tell you?
options: The statement is consistent and can be loaded
A line of 45.00 is missing or a balance is wrong
The bank charged 45.00 of unreported interest
The closing balance includes pending entries only
questions.explanation: 12,500.00 + 1,738.25 = 14,238.25, not 14,283.25, so either a line is missing or a balance is wrong; a difference divisible by 9 also hints at transposed digits. Guessing a cause such as interest is exactly what the continuity check exists to prevent.

questions.question: An MT940 :61: line has the mark RC and amount 3250,75. How is it normalized?
options: As +3250.75, because C means credit
As -3250.75, because a reversed credit is a debit
As a zero amount, because it cancels the original
As +3250.75, flagged for manual review instead
questions.explanation: RC is a reversal of a credit, which takes the money back out, so its effect on the balance is a debit. Reading only the C would mis-sign it and break continuity by twice the amount. camt.053 expresses the same thing with RvslInd.

questions.question: A camt.053 contains a CRDT entry of 999.00 with status PDNG. What should the parser do with it?
options: Include it, since the bank reported it in the statement
Include it only if its value date is before the closing date
Reject the whole statement, since pending entries are invalid
Exclude it from the lines that move the booked balance
questions.explanation: Only BOOK entries move the booked balance that OPBD and CLBD report. Counting the pending entry would make opening plus movements differ from closing by 999.00. Pending entries are valid information, so the statement should not be rejected.

questions.question: A BAI2 parser ignores 88 records. Which failure follows first in production?
options: Amounts are read with the wrong sign for type codes over 399
Descriptions lose their continuation, and record counts fail
The control totals no longer match because amounts are dropped
The as-of date is lost because it is carried on 88 records
questions.explanation: 88 records continue the previous record; for a 16 detail they carry the rest of the text, often the invoice number reconciliation needs. The trailer record counts include 88 lines, so a parser that checks them also fails. 88s on 16 records carry text, not amounts or dates.

questions.question: Why does the model mark an OFX statement with openingReported = false?
options: OFX reports only a closing balance, so a derived opening makes the check a tautology
OFX opening balances use a different sign convention from the other three formats
OFX statements cover only one day, so there is no meaningful opening to report
OFX amounts are decimals, so the opening balance cannot be represented exactly
questions.explanation: OFX gives LEDGERBAL and no opening; computing opening as closing minus movements guarantees the within-statement check passes, so it proves nothing. Marking it lets code and people rely on cross-download checks instead. OFX decimals convert exactly to minor units.

questions.question: Day 1 closes at 14,238.25 and day 2 opens at 14,250.75; each statement is internally continuous. What failed?
options: Nothing, since each statement passed its own continuity check
Day 2's parser mis-signed a 12.50 debit as a credit line
Day 1 is missing a 12.50 line that the bank booked late
Something changed the balance between statements without a line
questions.explanation: The chain invariant says each closing must equal the next opening. A 12.50 gap with both statements internally consistent means the balance moved between them with no line, such as a reversed fee or a missing statement. A mis-signed line or a missing day-1 line would break that statement's own continuity.
